reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Rulemaking based on substantial evidence on the record
headings.reviewNote: Requires state agencies to propose rules based on substantial evidence on the record and a finding that the rule is necessary to carry out the authorizing statute's purposes.

headings.title: Agency procedures and criteria for determining statutory necessity
headings.reviewNote: Requires agencies to adopt rule-necessity procedures based on reasonably available empirical data, including an assessment of rule effectiveness and costs to the state and affected public or private entities.

headings.title: Public internet website access to proposed rules
headings.reviewNote: Requires each state agency to place a 'proposed rules' homepage hyperlink providing proposed rule text/fiscal notes, a neutral 100-word summary, and Register/incorporated-material links within one business day of publication.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all three subsections and subdivisions for 536.016. Verified accuracy of titles and refined notes (including empirical data/cost assessment in subsection 2 and one-business-day website posting in subsection 3).

headings.title: Thirty legislative day delay on effective date of final rules
headings.reviewNote: Delays the effective date of a final order of rulemaking until expiration of thirty legislative days of a regular session after filing with JCAR and the secretary of state (contingent effective date; see subsection 2).

headings.title: Contingent effective date tied to Executive Order 97-97
headings.reviewNote: Makes this section effective twenty calendar days after specified contingencies regarding Executive Order 97-97 or invalidation of § 536.024 unless approved by concurrent resolution; source Revisor's note reports contingencies have not occurred.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections and Revisor's contingent-effective-date note (contingencies regarding Executive Order 97-97 have not occurred) for 536.019. Verified accuracy of titles and notes.

headings.title: Notice of proposed rulemaking filed with secretary of state
headings.reviewNote: Requires filing proposed rulemaking and final orders with the secretary of state for Register publication (with hunting/fishing and federal education plan exceptions), § 536.024 compliance, and legislative disapproval rules.

headings.title: Mandatory contents of notice of proposed rulemaking
headings.reviewNote: Lists six required contents of a notice of proposed rulemaking, including explanation, legal authority, rule text/incorporated material rules, rescission info, 30-day comment notice, and hearing notice.

headings.title: Discretionary agency hearings on proposed administrative rules
headings.reviewNote: Permits a state agency issuing a notice of proposed rulemaking to order a hearing, while making hearings unnecessary unless otherwise required by law.

headings.title: Subsequent notice of hearing after initial publication
headings.reviewNote: Requires an agency that initially proposed a rule without a hearing but later desires one to withdraw the earlier notice and file a new notice at least thirty days before the hearing.

headings.title: Ninety-day deadline for filing final order of rulemaking
headings.reviewNote: Requires filing a final order of rulemaking within ninety days after comment close or hearing (tolled during executive-order abeyance), or the proposed rule lapses and is void.

headings.title: Mandatory contents of final order of rulemaking
headings.reviewNote: Lists five required contents of a final order of rulemaking: Register citation, explanation of changes, changed text, summary of comments/testimony and agency findings, and legal authority.

headings.title: Nullity of administrative rules adopted without statutory compliance
headings.reviewNote: Except as provided in section 536.025, renders any rule, amendment, or rescission null, void, and unenforceable unless made in accordance with this section.

headings.title: Code of State Regulations publication and thirty-day effective date
headings.reviewNote: Requires publishing adopted rules in full in the Code of State Regulations with effective date at least thirty days after publication (or ten days after filing for specified hunting/fishing rules).

headings.title: Attorney fees for agency action based on unpromulgated rule
headings.reviewNote: Requires awarding reasonable attorney's fees (capped at amount in controversy) to a prevailing nonstate party after prior written notice when agency action relied on an unpromulgated rule, including via Cole County suit if agency grants prior relief.

headings.title: Department of revenue letter rulings exception to fee shifting
headings.reviewNote: Exempts the department of revenue from subsection 9 if it implements binding three-year letter rulings, makes unfavorable rulings nonbinding and unappealable, and requires periodic redacted publication subject to appropriations.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 10 subsections and subdivisions for 536.021. Verified accuracy of titles and refined notes (including hunting/fishing and federal education exceptions in subsection 1, 30-day effective date in subsection 8, and Cole County fee action in subsection 9).

headings.title: Notice of suspension or termination of administrative rules
headings.reviewNote: Requires a state agency to immediately file notice with the secretary of state if any rule or portion of a rule is suspended or terminated by the governor, a court, or other authority.

headings.title: Contents and format of notice of rule suspension or termination
headings.reviewNote: Requires the notice, in secretary-of-state format, to state the rule title/number, action taken, affected parties, effective date, suspension duration, and other necessary public information.

headings.title: New notice required when suspension or termination details change
headings.reviewNote: Requires the state agency to immediately file a new notice with the secretary of state in the same manner if any action changes information in the initial notice.

headings.title: Register publication and Code of State Regulations updates
headings.reviewNote: Directs the secretary of state to print notices in the Missouri Register as soon as practicable, insert suspension/termination material in the Code of State Regulations, and permits removing terminated rules.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all four subsections and effective date (6-27-97) for 536.022. Corrected shifted/fabricated subsections 3 (new notice upon changed information) and 4 (Register publication, CSR insertion, and optional removal of terminated rules).

headings.title: Secretary of state uniform procedures for indexing and publishing rules
headings.reviewNote: Directs the secretary of state to prescribe, furnish to agencies, and permanently maintain uniform procedures for numbering, indexing, form, and publication of rules, notices, and orders.

headings.title: Rejection of filings not conforming to uniform procedures
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits accepting any rule, notice of proposed rulemaking, or final order of rulemaking for filing with the secretary of state unless it conforms to uniform procedures.

headings.title: Agency rule describing organization, operations, and public access
headings.reviewNote: Requires each state agency to adopt as a rule a description of its organization, general courses/methods of operation, and public information/submission procedures, with substantial changes made under chapter 536.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all three subsections and history notes for 536.023. Replaced fabricated subsection 3 ('monthly administrative rules bulletin') with actual text requiring each state agency to adopt its organization and public-access description as a rule.

headings.title: Substantive rule validity contingent on procedural compliance
headings.reviewNote: Makes the grant of rulemaking authority and validity of agency rules promulgated after June 3, 1994 contingent upon agency compliance with this section.

headings.title: Concurrent submission of proposed rules to joint committee
headings.reviewNote: Requires concurrent submission of proposed rules to the joint committee on administrative rules upon filing with the secretary of state and permits committee hearings at any time.

headings.title: Thirty-day committee review wait before filing final rulemaking order
headings.reviewNote: Bars filing a final order of rulemaking with the secretary of state until thirty days after receipt by the joint committee, during which the committee may hold hearings.

headings.title: Committee comments and recommendations published in Missouri Register
headings.reviewNote: Permits the joint committee to file comments or recommendations on a proposed or final order of rulemaking with the secretary of state for publication in the Missouri Register.

headings.title: Committee referral of rule comments to appropriations committees
headings.reviewNote: Permits the joint committee to refer comments or recommendations concerning a rule to the House appropriations and budget committees and Senate appropriations committee for further action.

headings.title: Exemption for labor and industrial relations commission rules
headings.reviewNote: Provides that this section does not apply to rules adopted by the labor and industrial relations commission.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all six subsections and cross-reference (§ 287.811) for 536.024. Replaced completely fabricated subsections 3 through 6 with actual provisions on 30-day JCAR wait, JCAR Register comments, referral to appropriations committees, and Labor and Industrial Relations Commission exemption.

headings.title: Emergency rulemaking authority upon finding of immediate danger
headings.reviewNote: Permits making, amending, or rescinding a rule without § 536.021 procedures only upon finding immediate danger to public health/safety/welfare or compelling governmental interest, with fairness, constitutional compliance, and limited scope.

headings.title: Filing emergency rule text, fiscal notes, and supporting findings
headings.reviewNote: Requires filing rule text, §§ 536.200/536.205 fiscal notes, and supporting facts/findings with the secretary of state and JCAR (plus written certification for compelling governmental interest).

headings.title: Secretary of state publication, three-day notice, and compliance review
headings.reviewNote: Directs the secretary of state to publish emergency materials in the Register, email registered subscribers and post online within three business days, and reject noncompliant rules.

headings.title: Committee comments and recommendations published in Missouri Register
headings.reviewNote: Permits the joint committee to file comments or recommendations concerning a proposed or final order of rulemaking with the secretary of state for publication in the Missouri Register.

headings.title: Committee referral of rule comments to appropriations committees
headings.reviewNote: Permits the joint committee to refer comments or recommendations concerning a rule to the House appropriations and budget committee and Senate appropriations committee.

headings.title: Judicial review of emergency rules and secretary of state immunity
headings.reviewNote: Designates rules under this section as 'emergency rules' subject to judicial review under section 536.050 or other review, and immunizes the secretary of state and employees acting in scope of employment.

headings.title: Maximum effective duration of emergency administrative rules
headings.reviewNote: Requires stating the effective interval, caps emergency rules at 180 calendar days or 30 legislative days (whichever is longer), and defines 'legislative day'.

headings.title: Prohibition on renewal or consecutive identical emergency rules
headings.reviewNote: Bars renewing an emergency rule or adopting consecutive emergency rules with substantially the same effect, while allowing adoption of an identical rule under normal procedures.

headings.title: Minimum ten-business-day effective date and agency termination
headings.reviewNote: Provides that emergency rules may take effect not less than ten business days after filing (or later if specified) and may be terminated anytime by agency order published in the Register.

headings.title: Fee awards against agency for improper adoption of emergency rules
headings.reviewNote: Requires awarding reasonable fees and expenses to a prevailing nonstate party when an administrative or judicial fact finder finds an emergency rule was improperly adopted, including via Cole County suit if agency grants prior relief.

headings.title: Definitions under emergency rulemaking provisions
headings.reviewNote: Defines 'prevails' and 'reasonable fees and expenses' for purposes of this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 11 subsections, subdivisions, and cross-reference (§ 287.811) for 536.025. Replaced shifted/fabricated subsections 3 through 6 with actual provisions on SOS publication/3-day email/website/compliance review, JCAR Register comments, appropriations referral, and judicial review/SOS immunity.

headings.title: Public comment solicitation on prospective agency rules
headings.reviewNote: Permits an agency to solicit public comments on a rule under consideration and file a notice for publication in the Missouri Register stating rule number, subject matter, and comment instructions.

headings.title: Appointment of advisory rulemaking committees
headings.reviewNote: Permits each agency to appoint committees to comment on prospective rules and requires publishing committee membership at least annually in the Missouri Register.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections and effective date (6-27-97) for 536.026. Verified accuracy of titles and refined notes.

headings.title: Contingent delegation of authority to propose rules
headings.reviewNote: Makes agency authority to propose substantive rules contingent on chapter 536 compliance and general assembly review, 30-legislative-day delay, and disapproval/annulment power (contingent effective date; see subsection 13).

headings.title: Substantive rules ineffective pending legislative review
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits any substantive rule or portion thereof from taking effect until the final order of rulemaking is reviewed by the general assembly.

headings.title: Filing proposed rules with joint committee and agency cooperation
headings.reviewNote: Requires first filing notices of proposed rulemaking with JCAR, permits committee hearings at any time, and requires agency cooperation with witnesses, documents, and information.

headings.title: Thirty legislative day delay on effective date of proposed orders
headings.reviewNote: Bars a proposed order of rulemaking from taking effect before expiration of thirty legislative days of a regular session after filing with the secretary of state and JCAR.

headings.title: Joint committee recommendation to disapprove and annul rules
headings.reviewNote: Permits JCAR by majority vote after hearings to recommend disapproval and annulment of substantive rules on six enumerated nonexclusive grounds.

headings.title: Judicial admissibility of committee disapproval reports
headings.reviewNote: Makes any JCAR recommendation or report under subsection 5 admissible in judicial proceedings and entitled to judicial notice without further proof.

headings.title: Concurrent resolution disapproving and annulling proposed rules
headings.reviewNote: Permits the general assembly to adopt a concurrent resolution under Article IV, Section 8 of the Missouri Constitution to disapprove and annul any rule or portion thereof.

headings.title: Deemed approval of proposed rules absent legislative disapproval
headings.reviewNote: Deems any rule not disapproved within thirty legislative days approved and permits the secretary of state to publish the final order of rulemaking as soon as practicable thereafter.

headings.title: Publication hold and Register notice for disapproval resolutions
headings.reviewNote: Bars publishing an order of rulemaking pending gubernatorial action or veto override under Article III, Section 32, and requires Register publication of disapproved and annulled rules.

headings.title: Nonseverability of legislative delegation and review mechanisms
headings.reviewNote: Declares this section, § 536.021, and § 536.025 nonseverable notwithstanding § 1.140, revoking rulemaking authority and nullifying proposed rules if legislative oversight powers are held invalid.

headings.title: Legislative authority to enact rules directly by statute
headings.reviewNote: Preserves general assembly power to adopt, amend, or annul proposed rules by bill or concurrent resolution within thirty legislative days, superseding and barring publication of the proposed order.

headings.title: Revocation of effective rules by legislative enactment
headings.reviewNote: Permits revoking any effective rule by bill or Article IV, Section 8 concurrent resolution on JCAR recommendation, with notice published in the Missouri Register.

headings.title: Contingent effective date tied to Executive Order 97-97
headings.reviewNote: Makes this section effective twenty calendar days after specified Executive Order 97-97 or § 536.024 contingencies unless approved by concurrent resolution; source Revisor's note reports contingencies have not occurred.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 13 subsections, subdivisions, and Revisor's contingent-effective-date note (Executive Order 97-97 contingencies have not occurred) for 536.028. Refined subsection 9 note (governor signature/veto wait and Register publication of disapproved rules) and verified all titles.

headings.title: Establishment of Code of State Regulations
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the 'Code of State Regulations' published in a format and medium prescribed from time to time by the secretary of state.

headings.title: Mandatory inclusion of all effective state agency rules
headings.reviewNote: Requires the code to contain full text of all effective state agency rules, be revised at least monthly (since Sept. 1, 1990), and allows agency or SOS annotations to rulings, opinions, and decisions.

headings.title: Publication format and medium of Code of State Regulations
headings.reviewNote: Requires the Code of State Regulations to be published in a format and medium prescribed by the secretary of state.

headings.title: Incorporation by reference of federal regulations and industry standards
headings.reviewNote: Permits incorporating federal or recognized organization standards by reference without future amendments, except hospital licensure rules under ch. 197 may incorporate later Medicare conditions and life safety code updates.

headings.title: Agency duty to maintain incorporated reference materials
headings.reviewNote: Requires agencies to keep incorporated materials at headquarters for public inspection/copying at actual reproduction cost and permits the secretary of state to omit unduly cumbersome or expensive incorporated material.

headings.title: Mandatory judicial notice of Code of State Regulations
headings.reviewNote: Directs Missouri courts to take judicial notice, without proof, of the contents of the Code of State Regulations.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all six subsections and hospital-licensure subdivisions for 536.031. Verified accuracy of titles and refined notes (including monthly revision since Sept. 1, 1990 and optional omission of cumbersome incorporated material).

headings.title: Public sale and subscription charges for register and code
headings.reviewNote: Requires making copies or subscriptions of the Register or Code available to the public for a reasonable charge established by the secretary of state not exceeding actual publishing and delivery cost.

headings.title: Deposit of publication sales revenues to general revenue
headings.reviewNote: Requires all fees collected from sales of the Missouri Register or Code of State Regulations by the secretary of state to be deposited to general revenue.

headings.title: Secretary of state authority to correct clerical and spelling errors
headings.reviewNote: Permits the secretary of state to correct typographical or spelling errors in the publication of any rule, notice of proposed rulemaking, or order of rulemaking.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all three subsections and history notes for 536.033. Verified accuracy of titles and removed unsupported 'grammatical' from subsection 3 note.

headings.title: Permanent public record status of filed rules and orders
headings.reviewNote: Requires permanent retention and public inspection at all reasonable times for all rules or executive orders filed with the secretary of state under sections 536.015 to 536.043.

headings.title: Publication of post-January 1, 2003 executive orders in Register
headings.reviewNote: Requires all executive orders issued after January 1, 2003 to be published in the Missouri Register.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections and history notes for 536.035. Refined subsection 2 to include the January 1, 2003 cutoff date.

headings.title: Creation and legislative composition of Committee on Administrative Rules
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the permanent joint Committee on Administrative Rules with five senators and five representatives, capping major-party representation at three members per house.

headings.title: Organization and selection of committee officers
headings.reviewNote: Directs the committee to meet within ten days of creation, select a chairman and vice chairman from different chambers, sets majority quorum, and allows meetings at chairman's call.

headings.title: Committee duty to review all administrative agency rules
headings.reviewNote: Directs the committee to review all rules promulgated after January 1, 1976 (except Labor and Industrial Relations Commission rules) and permits taking necessary action including hearings.

headings.title: Compensation and actual expenses of committee members
headings.reviewNote: Provides no additional compensation beyond legislative salary, while permitting reimbursement of necessary meeting expenses from the joint contingent fund.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all four subsections and cross-reference (§ 287.811) for 536.037. Refined subsection 3 note to include post-January 1, 1976 scope and Labor and Industrial Relations Commission exemption.

headings.title: Declaratory judgment actions and venue for challenging rules
headings.reviewNote: Extends declaratory judgment power to rule validity or threatened application without prior agency request, sets venue in Cole County or plaintiff's residence/registered office, and preserves other judicial relief.

headings.title: Exceptions to exhausting administrative remedies
headings.reviewNote: Waives administrative exhaustion for inadequate authority/remedy, pure legal/constitutional issues, irreparable harm (excluding chs. 288, 302, 303), or small business § 536.300/§ 536.303 claims (note: § 536.303 repealed in 2024).

headings.title: Award of reasonable fees and expenses to prevailing nonstate party
headings.reviewNote: Mandates awarding reasonable fees and expenses (as defined in § 536.085) to a nonstate party who prevails in a subsection 1 declaratory judgment action.

headings.title: Thirty-day application deadline and itemized fee statement
headings.reviewNote: Requires a nonstate party seeking fees to apply within thirty days of final disposition to the rendering court with proof of prevailing eligibility and itemized attorney/expert time and rate statements.

headings.title: Forum for fee application and stay pending state merits appeal
headings.reviewNote: Directs filing with the court where the party prevailed, provides that filing does not stay appeal time, and stays fee decisions while the state appeals the underlying merits.

headings.title: Reduction or denial of fee award for unreasonable protraction
headings.reviewNote: Permits the court to reduce or deny a fee award to the extent the prevailing nonstate party unduly and unreasonably protracted final resolution of the controversy.

headings.title: Separate written fee decision with findings and conclusions
headings.reviewNote: Requires the court's fee decision to be in writing, separate from the merits judgment, include findings, conclusions, and reasons, and makes it final and appealable.

headings.title: Appellate review of fee determinations and appropriation payment
headings.reviewNote: Allows either party to appeal fee determinations on the record below under arbitrary/capricious or legal-error review, makes awards payable from appropriations, and requires the agency to request an appropriation.

headings.title: Standing of general assembly or joint committee to intervene
headings.reviewNote: Grants the general assembly or its designee (by default JCAR upon majority vote) standing to intervene in existing rule challenges without imposing any duty to intervene.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all nine subsections, repealed § 536.303 footnote (S.B. 894 & 825, 2024), and 1982/1993 annotations for 536.050. Replaced completely fabricated/shifted subsections 2 through 9 with actual statutory provisions on exhaustion exceptions, prevailing-party fees, 30-day application, appeal stay, protraction reduction, written decision, fee appeals/appropriations, and General Assembly/JCAR intervention.

headings.title: Responsive pleading deadlines and types before hearing commission
headings.reviewNote: Requires responsive pleadings (answers, motions to dismiss, motions for more definite statement) before the administrative hearing commission within circuit-court civil answer limits unless extended.

headings.title: One-week bench ruling or memorandum decision on joint request
headings.reviewNote: Requires the administrative hearing commission, on request of all parties and waiver of § 536.090, to issue a bench ruling or memorandum decision within one week of hearing conclusion or request, whichever is later.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections and history note for 536.068. Corrected fabricated deadlines in both subsections (civil circuit-court answer time limits in subsection 1, not 30 days; one-week bench ruling/memorandum decision in subsection 2, not 90 days).

headings.title: Use and taking of depositions in contested administrative cases
headings.reviewNote: Allows parties in contested cases before constitutionally or statutorily created agencies to take and use depositions as in circuit-court civil actions; source footnote notes word 'sued' appears in original rolls.

headings.title: Agency civil discovery rules and circuit court enforcement limits
headings.reviewNote: Permits contested-case agencies to adopt and enforce civil discovery rules, while requiring circuit-court order after notice and hearing to enforce physical/mental exams, nonconsensual land entry, or contempt.

headings.title: Hearing commission rules for informal disposition of contested cases
headings.reviewNote: Directs the administrative hearing commission to adopt rules under § 536.021 after public hearing for informal disposition by stipulation, consent order, settlement, default, judgment on pleadings, or summary judgment.

headings.title: Rule effectiveness contingent on joint committee approval and review
headings.reviewNote: Makes effectiveness of chapter 536 rules and legislative rulemaking delegation dependent upon joint committee on administrative rules approval, review, and suspension pending legislative ratification.

headings.title: Concurrent submission of proposed rules to joint committee
headings.reviewNote: Requires agencies filing proposed rules with the secretary of state to concurrently submit them to the joint committee, which may hold hearings at any time.

headings.title: Thirty-day committee review wait, deemed approval, and early approval
headings.reviewNote: Bars filing final orders of rulemaking until thirty days after committee receipt (deemed approved if not disapproved), while allowing earlier filing if the committee approves prior to expiration.

headings.title: Grounds for joint committee suspension of rulemaking order
headings.reviewNote: Permits the joint committee by majority vote to suspend an order of rulemaking before filing on five grounds: no statutory authority, public health/safety/welfare emergency, state law conflict, changed circumstances, or arbitrary/capricious.

headings.title: Bar on filing or publishing committee-disapproved rule portions
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits the filing agency from filing and the secretary of state from publishing in the Missouri Register any portion of a rule disapproved by the joint committee.

headings.title: Committee report and thirty-legislative-day ratification by resolution
headings.reviewNote: Requires reporting committee disapprovals to the senate and house and bars disapproved rules from taking effect if both houses ratify the committee's act by resolution within thirty legislative days.

headings.title: Legislative suspension or revocation of adopted rules
headings.reviewNote: Permits suspending or revoking any adopted rule by bill or Article IV, Section 8 concurrent resolution on committee recommendation, with notice published in the Missouri Register.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all 10 subsections, original-rolls footnote (*word 'sued' in subsection 1), cross-reference (§ 287.811), and 1998 St. Charles annotation for 536.073. Replaced completely fabricated/shifted subsections 2 through 9 with actual statutory text on agency discovery rules/court enforcement, AHC informal-disposition rules, and JCAR review/suspension/ratification procedures.

headings.title: Party entitlement to present oral argument and written briefs
headings.reviewNote: Entitles each party in a contested case to present oral arguments or written briefs at or after the hearing, to be heard or read by each deciding agency official.

headings.title: Deciding official review of evidence or record and party waiver
headings.reviewNote: Requires each deciding official to hear all evidence, read the full record, or personally consider record portions cited in arguments/briefs, unless waived by written or on-record oral stipulation.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections and 1976 PSC annotation for 536.080. Refined subsection 2 to reflect the three statutory compliance options and party waiver by stipulation.

headings.title: Award of reasonable fees and expenses to prevailing parties
headings.reviewNote: Mandates awarding reasonable fees and expenses to a party prevailing in an agency proceeding or arising civil action by or against the state unless the state's position was substantially justified or special circumstances make an award unjust.

headings.title: Inclusion of agency proceeding fees in judicial review awards
headings.reviewNote: Requires a court awarding fees to a party prevailing on judicial review to include reasonable fees and expenses incurred during the agency proceeding unless the state's agency position was substantially justified or unjust.

headings.title: Thirty-day fee application deadline and substantial justification review
headings.reviewNote: Sets a thirty-day fee application deadline with itemized statements and non-justification allegation, bars presuming non-justification from state loss, and limits review to the underlying record and targeted fee hearing.

headings.title: Forum for fee application and stay pending state merits appeal
headings.reviewNote: Directs filing fee applications with the prevailing forum (agency or court), provides filing does not stay appeal time, and defers fee decisions while the state appeals the underlying merits.

headings.title: Reduction or denial of fee awards for unreasonable protraction
headings.reviewNote: Permits the court or agency to reduce or deny any award to the extent the prevailing party unduly and unreasonably protracted final resolution.

headings.title: Requirement of separate written decision on fee application
headings.reviewNote: Requires a separate written decision with findings, conclusions, and reasons on fee applications, which is final and subject to appeal or judicial review.

headings.title: Judicial review, appeals, and appropriation payment of fee awards
headings.reviewNote: Provides 30-day judicial review of agency fee rulings and civil appeals of court fee rulings on the record below (see 1999 Greenbriar Hills annotation), with H.B. 143 ('this act*') awards payable from agency-requested appropriations.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all seven subsections, H.B. 143 'this act*' footnote, and 1998 McGhee / 1999 Greenbriar Hills annotations for 536.087. Refined subsection 7 title/note to include both agency judicial review and civil-action appeals plus appropriation payment.

headings.title: Thirty-day deadline for filing judicial review petition
headings.reviewNote: Permits instituting judicial review by filing a petition in the circuit court of proper venue within thirty days after mailing or delivery of notice of the agency's final decision.

headings.title: Rehearing tolling and petition service without summons
headings.reviewNote: Allows filing without seeking rehearing (tolling the 30-day period if an authorized rehearing motion is filed), bars summons issuance, and requires delivery or registered mailing of petition copies with filed proof.

headings.title: Venue for judicial review and discretionary intervention
headings.reviewNote: Sets venue in Cole County or plaintiff's residence/registered office, except real-property cases must be filed where the real property lies, and permits discretionary intervention by interested persons.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all three subsections and 1969-1984 annotations for 536.110. Expanded subsection 2 to cover delivery/registered-mail service (no summons) and subsection 3 to cover real property venue exception and discretionary intervention.

headings.title: Thirty-day deadline and contents of agency record on review
headings.reviewNote: Requires filing the agency record within thirty days of petition filing (or extended time) via stipulated record, agreed statement, or complete transcript, always including the decision, order, findings, and conclusions.

headings.title: Certification, reproduction, and transmission of original exhibits
headings.reviewNote: Requires agency certification and suitable reproduction of the record, while permitting sending originals or copies of documents/exhibits with agency permission instead of copying them into the record.

headings.title: Agency resolution of record correctness and cost sanctions
headings.reviewNote: Directs the agency to decide and certify record correctness if a party refuses to agree, and permits the court to tax added expense as costs against a party refusing a proper shortening of the record.

headings.title: Filing, direct agency transmittal, and record corrections
headings.reviewNote: Requires filing by plaintiff or direct agency transmittal on plaintiff's request (mandatory for original documents), and permits court-ordered or permitted subsequent corrections or additions to the record.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all four subsections and subdivisions for 536.130. Refined subsection 3 note (agency decides correctness; court may tax costs for refusal to shorten record; corrections/additions are in subsection 4).

headings.title: Non-jury judicial review upon petition and agency record
headings.reviewNote: Requires the court to hear the case without a jury and, except as provided in subsection 4, upon the petition and agency record filed.

headings.title: Seven grounds of judicial inquiry and minimum review scope
headings.reviewNote: Lists seven grounds of judicial review inquiry (constitutional, authority/jurisdiction, substantial evidence, unauthorized by law, unlawful procedure, arbitrary/capricious, abuse of discretion) as a minimum scope in all contested cases.

headings.title: De novo interpretation without deference to state agencies
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits courts and hearing officers from deferring to a state agency's interpretation of state statutes, rules, or subregulatory documents, mandates de novo interpretation, and resolves remaining doubt in favor of limiting agency power and maximizing individual liberty.

headings.title: Additional evidence, remand, and procedural irregularity hearings
headings.reviewNote: Permits hearing additional evidence when entitled to weigh facts, or remanding when not, for diligently unproducible or improperly excluded evidence, and allows hearing evidence of off-record procedural irregularities or unfairness.

headings.title: Judicial judgment and limits on substituting agency discretion
headings.reviewNote: Directs judgment affirming, reversing, or modifying the agency order (with optional reconsideration or further-action orders), barring substitution of discretion unless the agency decision was arbitrary or capricious.

headings.title: Appellate review as in other civil actions
headings.reviewNote: Provides that appeals may be taken from the judgment of the court as in other civil cases.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all six subsections, 2025 S.B. 221 de novo/no-deference amendment, and 1999/2004 annotations for 536.140. Corrected shifted subsection 1 (non-jury review on petition and record) and replaced fabricated subsection 3 with the 2025 no-deference / de novo interpretation standard.

headings.title: Judicial review of noncontested administrative decisions
headings.reviewNote: Permits review of non-reviewable administrative decisions determining legal rights, duties, or privileges by injunction, certiorari, mandamus, prohibition, or other action, with judicial fact-finding and limits on substituting lawful discretion.

headings.title: Inapplicability to contested cases under sections 536.100 to 536.140
headings.reviewNote: Provides that nothing in this section applies to contested cases reviewable pursuant to sections 536.100 to 536.140.

headings.title: Preservation of summary powers, court jurisdiction, and other remedies
headings.reviewNote: Provides that this section does not impair lawful summary-action powers of administrative officers/bodies or limit court jurisdiction or other available remedies.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all three subsections and 1972/1975/1979 annotations for 536.150. Replaced completely fabricated subsections 2 ('hearing and judgment') and 3 ('appellate review') with actual exclusions for contested cases and preservation of summary powers and remedies.

headings.title: Schedule for periodic review of agency rules by title
headings.reviewNote: Establishes a staggered five-year periodic rule review schedule by Code of State Regulations title groups beginning July 1, 2015 through July 1, 2019 and every five years thereafter.

headings.title: Joint committee notification of agency review in Missouri Register
headings.reviewNote: Directs JCAR to publish review notifications in the Missouri Register identifying titles under review, 60-day comment deadline, comment identification rules, and agency designees.

headings.title: Agency designation of contact person to receive public comments
headings.reviewNote: Requires state agencies to provide JCAR with contact information for the agency designee assigned to receive subsection 2 public comments.

headings.title: Mandatory contents of agency periodic rule review report
headings.reviewNote: Lists eight required elements for each agency's periodic review report, including necessity, obsolescence, overlap/conflict, less restrictive alternatives, burden reduction, § 536.031 incorporation, small business purpose, and comment summary/responses.

headings.title: Report filing, website access, and voiding of delinquent rules
headings.reviewNote: Requires electronic filing by June 30 with JCAR and the small business regulatory fairness board plus website posting, and voids delinquent rules after 60 legislative days unless cured within 90 days of Register delinquency notice.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all five subsections and subdivisions for 536.175. Refined subsection 5 title/note to include delinquency notices and voiding of unreviewed rules.

headings.title: Fiscal notes required for rules affecting public expenditure
headings.reviewNote: Requires a fiscal note with § 575.060 director declaration when a proposed or emergency rule costs state/local public entities over $500 in the aggregate, or a declaration that costs are under $500.

headings.title: Fiscal note duration for emergency administrative rules
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a fiscal note for an emergency rule filed under section 536.025 shall only reflect fiscal costs for the duration of the emergency rule.

headings.title: First-year actual cost publication when estimates exceeded
headings.reviewNote: Requires publishing original estimated and actual first-year costs in the Register within 90 days after fiscal year close if actual costs exceed estimates by 10% or more (or exceed $500 under a declaration), or the rule is void.

headings.title: Publication of estimated public costs in Missouri Register
headings.reviewNote: Requires publishing aggregate estimated public costs in the Missouri Register contemporary with and adjacent to the rulemaking notice, or the rule is void.

headings.title: Five-year limitation period on challenges for fiscal note noncompliance
headings.reviewNote: Requires commencing any challenge to a rule based on failure to meet this section's requirements within five years after the rule's effective date.

headings.title: Historical compliance provision for pre-1994 administrative rules
headings.reviewNote: Permits curing omitted fiscal notes on rules published before June 3, 1994 by publishing cross-referenced fiscal notes before August 28, 1995 so those rules are not void.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all six subsections and history notes for 536.200. Verified accuracy of titles and refined notes (including $500 aggregate threshold, § 575.060 declaration, and voiding consequences in subsections 3-4).

headings.title: Fiscal notes required for rules affecting private entities
headings.reviewNote: Requires filing a private-entity fiscal note with affected-class counts, business classifications, and aggregate compliance cost estimates when a proposed or emergency rule costs private entities over $500 in the aggregate.

headings.title: Fiscal note duration for private impact of emergency rules
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a fiscal note for an emergency rule filed under section 536.025 shall only reflect fiscal costs for the duration of the emergency rule.

headings.title: Publication of private entity fiscal note in Missouri Register
headings.reviewNote: Requires publishing the fiscal note in the Missouri Register contemporary with and adjacent to the notice of rulemaking, or the rule is void.

headings.title: Five-year limitation period on challenges for private fiscal note errors
headings.reviewNote: Requires commencing any challenge to a rule for failure to meet this section's requirements no later than five years after the rule's effective date.

headings.title: Historical compliance provision for pre-1994 private fiscal notes
headings.reviewNote: Permits curing omitted private fiscal notes on rules published before June 3, 1994 by publishing the required fiscal note before August 28, 1995 so those rules are not void.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all five subsections, subdivisions, and 1994 Mo. Hosp. Assn. annotation for 536.205. Verified accuracy of titles and refined notes.

headings.title: Agency determination of proposed rule effect on small business
headings.reviewNote: Requires agencies before submitting proposed rules (excluding § 536.025 emergency rules and Mo. Const. Art. IV, § 45 rules) to determine small-business impact and less-restrictive alternatives in addition to §§ 536.200-536.210 fiscal notes.

headings.title: Small business impact statement preparation and flexible alternatives
headings.reviewNote: Requires considering flexible compliance methods, submitting a seven-element small business impact statement to the SOS, JCAR, and board before hearing notice, with § 536.205 fiscal-note cross-exceptions.

headings.title: Invalidity of proposed rules omitting required small business impact statement
headings.reviewNote: Renders proposed rules omitting a required small business impact statement invalid and unpublishable until provided, while allowing publication upon agency certification of no small-business economic impact.

headings.title: Exemptions for emergency, federally mandated, and codifying rules
headings.reviewNote: Exempts emergency, federally mandated, and existing-law-codifying rules from this section and § 536.320 (source footnote notes repealed § '536.020' in original rolls), while subjecting federally mandated rules to federal Regulatory Flexibility Act compliance.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked all four subsections, subdivisions, and original-rolls footnote (*section '536.020' in original rolls, repealed 1975) for 536.300. Corrected subsection 4 note (exempts rules substantially codifying existing federal or state law, not 'reducing regulatory burdens') and documented the original-rolls footnote.

headings.title: Discretionary waiver or reduction of penalties for small businesses
headings.reviewNote: Permits state agencies to consider waiving or reducing administrative penalties or fines against a small business upon 30-day correction, unintentional/excusable neglect, excusable rule misunderstanding, or self-identification.

headings.title: Circumstances precluding waiver of small business administrative penalties
headings.reviewNote: Bars subsection 1 waiver or reduction for lack of good faith, willful/criminal conduct, egregious violations, serious health/safety/environmental impact, non-waivable federal penalties, or continuing violation patterns.

entries.reviewSummary: Checked both subsections and all subdivisions for 536.320. Verified accuracy of titles and refined notes.
